proposed.sourceName: American Halal Foundation — Is Gelatin Halal? (Mohammad A. Hussaini, Executive Director)
proposed.paraphrase: The American Halal Foundation states that plant-derived gelling substitutes — agar-agar, carrageenan, and pectin — are halal by default because they are sourced from plants and involve no animal slaughter; the slaughter requirement that applies to animal gelatin does not apply to plant sources.

proposed.sourceName: Heliyon — Towards halal pharmaceutical: Exploring alternatives to animal-based ingredients (Herdiana et al.)
proposed.paraphrase: Peer-reviewed review describing agar-agar, carrageenan, pectin and other plant/algae-derived gelling agents as non-animal substitutes that constitute 100% halal ingredients, requiring no animal source or slaughter.

researcherNote: Plant origin involves no animal and no slaughter, so it satisfies even the strictest (zabiha) position. Two independent sources support seeded draft grade 1 (Halal). APPROVED by owner 2026-06-28.
